title: A first circuit
context: An original ESP32 DevKit: an LED, a button, and a 5 V PIR motion sensor module.
code:
LED anode   -> GPIO 2, cathode -> GND          (no resistor)
Button      -> between GPIO 34 and GND
PIR VCC     -> 5V,  PIR OUT -> GPIO 12,  PIR GND -> separate 5 V adapter's GND

button = Pin(34, Pin.IN, Pin.PULL_UP)

findings.d: The LED draws as much current as the pin can give: it can damage the pin or the LED. 220 Ω to 1 kΩ in series.
34 to 39 are input only, without pulls: `PULL_UP` does nothing and the input floats. Use another pin, or an external 10 kΩ pull-up.

findings.t: PIR on GPIO 12, a strapping pin
findings.d: If the sensor holds 12 high at reset, the flash voltage is set wrong and the board won't boot. Use a non-strapping pin.

findings.t: No shared ground with the PIR
findings.d: Its GND is on another adapter, so its output means nothing to the ESP32. Connect the grounds.
Many PIR modules output 3.3 V even on 5 V supply, but check: a 5 V output into the pin can damage it.

title: A main loop
context: Reads a sensor every 10 s and keeps the readings to send when the network's back.

findings.t: The readings list grows without bound
findings.d: Offline for a day, it fills the heap: MemoryError and a reset, losing everything. Keep a fixed-size buffer, or drop old readings.
Every time the network is OK, every reading ever taken is sent again. Clear what was sent.
One failed sensor read or send ends the loop, and the device does nothing until reset. Catch, log and continue.
ticks wrap around; the subtraction goes wrong eventually. `time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), start)`.
After a power cut it counts from 2000. Set it with ntptime first, or don't timestamp until it has worked.

title: Reading the probe
context: One DS18B20 in the fridge on GPIO 4.

findings.d: The conversion takes up to 750 ms; reading at once returns the last value, or 85.0 at power-up. `time.sleep_ms(750)` (or `await asyncio.sleep_ms(750)`).

findings.t: `ds.scan()[0]` raises when the probe is missing
findings.d: Unplugged or a broken wire: IndexError, and if uncaught, the main loop dies. Check for an empty scan and report an error.
85.0 and -127 are failure values, not temperatures. Reject them and anything implausible for a fridge.
Scan once at start and keep the rom; rescan only if reads fail.

title: umqtt on the board
code:
wlan = network.WLAN(network.STA_IF)
wlan.active(True)
wlan.connect("house", "hunter2")
while not wlan.isconnected():
    pass

c = MQTTClient("esp32", "jarvis", keepalive=60)
c.connect()
c.set_last_will(b"home/kitchen/fridge/status", b"offline")

while True:
    c.publish(b"home/kitchen/fridge/temp", str(temp()))
    time.sleep(300)

findings.t: Publishes every 5 minutes with a 60 s keepalive and no ping
findings.d: umqtt doesn't ping by itself. After 90 s of silence the broker drops the connection, and the next publish fails. Ping within the keepalive, or set the keepalive above the publish interval.
Any Wi-Fi or socket error raises out of the loop and the device stops for good. Wrap in a recover loop: Wi-Fi, connect, work; on OSError back off and start over.

findings.t: Will set after connect, and not retained
findings.d: The will is part of CONNECT: set it before `connect()`, with `retain=True`, and publish a retained "online" after.
The next board flashed from the same code evicts this one. Use `machine.unique_id()`.

findings.t: Wi-Fi wait with no timeout, password in the code
findings.d: A router reboot at power-up hangs it forever. Add a timeout; move the password to secrets.py, out of git.

findings.t: `jarvis` may not resolve on the board
findings.d: No mDNS by default. Use the Pi's LAN IP, with a fixed lease.

title: It resets when it connects
context: "The board boots, prints 'connecting to Wi-Fi', then resets. Over and over. Must be a Wi-Fi bug." It's on a 1 m thin USB cable from a laptop hub, with a relay module powered from its 3V3 pin.
code:
rst:0xc (SW_CPU_RESET)
...
connecting to Wi-Fi
Brownout detector was triggered
ets Jun  8 2016 00:22:57
rst:0xf (BROWNOUT_RST)

findings.t: It's power, not Wi-Fi: the log says brownout
findings.d: Wi-Fi's current peaks pull the voltage below the detector's threshold. Read the log before debugging code.
Both drop voltage under load. A short, thick cable into a proper USB charger.

findings.t: The relay coil on the 3V3 pin
findings.d: It draws a lot through the board's small regulator. Power it from 5 V (with a driver transistor), not the 3V3 rail.
A 100 µF or so across 3.3 V and GND smooths the peaks.

title: A battery sensor
context: A battery-powered balcony sensor on a dev board, meant to last months.
code:
count = 0

def main():
    global count
    count += 1
    wifi(SSID, PW)
    c = connect_mqtt()
    c.publish(b"home/balcony/temp", str(read()), qos=0)
    if count % 10 == 0:
        c.publish(b"home/balcony/battery", str(battery()))
    machine.deepsleep(60_000)

main()

findings.d: Deep sleep wake is a reset: count is always 1 and the battery is never reported. Keep it in RTC memory.
Joining Wi-Fi each wake dominates the battery: days, not months. Measure every minute if needed, but send every 10 to 15 minutes or on change.

findings.t: Sleeps right after a QoS 0 publish
findings.d: The message may not have left. Disconnect cleanly before sleeping.
Between wakes a dashboard has nothing to show. Retain them, with a timestamp.

findings.t: A dev board for a months-long battery
findings.d: Its regulator, USB chip and LED draw mA through every sleep. Use a board built for batteries, or measure first.

title: A watchdog that can't bite
context: "Added a watchdog so it never hangs."
code:
wdt = WDT(timeout=5000)
timer = Timer(0)
timer.init(period=1000, callback=lambda t: wdt.feed())

wifi(SSID, PW)
while True:
    c = connect_mqtt()
    publish_reading(c)
    time.sleep(60)

findings.d: The timer keeps feeding while the main loop is hung, so the watchdog never resets anything. Feed it in the main loop, after real work.

findings.t: A 5 s timeout with a 60 s sleep and a Wi-Fi connect
findings.d: Fed properly from the loop, it would reset a healthy device every cycle. Choose a timeout longer than the slowest healthy cycle, and sleep in short slices that feed.

findings.t: A new MQTT connection every minute
findings.d: `connect_mqtt()` in the loop opens a connection each cycle without closing the last. Connect once; reconnect on error.
Publish `machine.reset_cause()` at boot, so watchdog resets are visible.

title: An ESPHome file
context: A door sensor's YAML, committed to the repo.
code:
esphome:
  name: front door
esp32:
  board: esp32-c3-devkitm-1
wifi:
  ssid: house
  password: hunter2
mqtt:
  broker: jarvis
  topic_prefix: home/hall/door
binary_sensor:
  - platform: gpio
    pin: GPIO9
    name: Door

findings.d: Move them to secrets.yaml (`!secret wifi_password`) and keep that out of git.
Every change means taking the sensor off the door and plugging in USB.

findings.t: GPIO9 is a C3 strapping pin
findings.d: A door contact holding it low at reset puts the chip in download mode: it won't boot with the door in one position. Use another pin.

findings.t: No MQTT login, and a hostname
findings.d: Add `username`/`password` (its own user on the leaf), and use the Pi's IP; `jarvis` may not resolve on the board.
Add `mode: INPUT_PULLUP` (or `pullup: true`) and a `delayed_on_off` filter, or one door opening becomes several events.
`name: front door` becomes the hostname; use `front-door`.
